귀신들도 하나님을 믿고 떤다(약 2:19) — 그렇다면 구원 얻는 믿음은.en: The devils also believe, and tremble (James 2:19) — so how is saving faith different? This lecture dissects the three elements of faith that Protestantism has set out since the Reformation — knowledge, assent and trust — and uses the Greek expression "believing into Christ" and the picture of boarding an airplane to show that faith is not a conclusion of the head but a movement of one's whole being. It explains why repentance and faith are two directions of a single turning, why the Bible calls faith "obedience" (Romans 6:17; John 3:36; Romans 1:5; 16:26), and why the gospel is not an offer but a King's decree.

구원 얻는 믿음의 비밀 02 · 행함이 없으면 구원 취소인가, 바울과 야.en: The Secret of Saving Faith 02 · Is Salvation Canceled Without Works? Paul and James Are Not at War

루터가 '지푸라기 서신'이라 부른 야고보서 — '믿음으로 되는 줄 인정하.en: James, the book Luther called an "epistle of straw" — do "a man is justified by faith" (Romans 3:28) and "not by faith only" (James 2:24) really clash? This lecture looks at two cliffs — the Galatian church's "faith plus works" and the "cheap grace" Bonhoeffer warned against — and shows that Paul and James are aiming at different targets and speaking in different courts (the ground of salvation and the genuineness of faith). From the gap of about thirty years between Genesis 15 and 22 it confirms when Abraham was declared righteous, and through Ephesians 2:8–10 and the parable of the vine it shows that good works are not the root of salvation but its fruit. Finally it turns to the last piece of evidence shown by the thief on the cross: faith whose root is alive bears fruit even with nailed hands.

구원 얻는 믿음의 비밀 03 · 모세도 가나안에 못 들어갔다, 그러면 모.en: The Secret of Saving Faith 03 · Even Moses Couldn't Enter Canaan — So Did Moses Go to Heaven?

어린양의 피로 구원받은 이스라엘도 광야에서 불순종하다 가나안에 못 들어갔.en: Israel was saved by the blood of the lamb, yet disobeyed in the wilderness and could not enter Canaan — so if a believer complains, will he fail to reach heaven? This lecture separates what the Bible distinguishes: salvation (justification), rest and inheritance, and chastening. With "when I see the blood" (Exodus 12:13) and "once for all" (Hebrews 10:10) it confirms that the Passover was never once canceled. In Numbers 14 — "I have pardoned," yet "they shall not see the land" — it distinguishes forgiveness from consequences, and from the scene of Moses, who never entered Canaan, appearing in glory on the Mount of Transfiguration, it shows that Canaan is not heaven. The rest of Hebrews is entered by faith, ceasing from one's own works; and faith that holds fast to the end is not an admission fee but the fingerprint left on those who are already in Christ (Hebrews 3:14).

구원 얻는 믿음의 비밀 04 · 한 번 타락하면 끝인가 — 히브리서 6장.en: The Secret of Saving Faith 04 · Is One Fall the End? Hebrews 6 and the Final Word on Losing Salvation

'한 번 빛을 받고 타락한 자는 다시 회개하게 할 수 없다'는 히브리서.en: The final part of the series, for those who lose sleep over Hebrews 6 — that those "once enlightened" who fall away cannot be renewed again unto repentance. It first shows that reading this passage as loss of salvation, because of "cannot be renewed again," collides head-on with the restoration of Peter and David, and confirms that the context (leave the first principles and go on unto perfection) is a call to grow. The real reason restoration is impossible — there is no other way outside the sacrifice of Christ offered once for all — is explained with the picture of a single flight a day. It then dissects, in turn, the fire on the thorny ground (what burns is the thorns, not the field), the sinning "wilfully" of chapter 10 (not weakness but apostasy that denies the blood), and what Esau lost (not salvation but his inheritance). What happens when a child of God sins is not the reversal of the verdict but the Father's chastening — and the lecture closes with the gospel of double jeopardy, in which the Judge has become our Father.

특강 · 98분 몰아보기 구원 얻는 믿음의 비밀 — 한번 믿으면 영원히.en: Special · 98-Minute Binge-Watch: The Secret of Saving Faith — Once Saved, Always Saved, or Can It Be Lost? (01–04)

「구원 얻는 믿음의 비밀」 01~04편을 한 호흡으로 묶은 약 98분 총.en: A complete review of about 98 minutes that brings parts 01–04 of "The Secret of Saving Faith" together in one sitting. It starts from faith as trust that commits oneself to Christ — beyond the knowledge and assent even devils have — and as the heart's obedience to the King's decree (Part 1); goes on to Paul and James speaking of different targets and courts between two cliffs (Part 2); the distinction between salvation, inheritance and chastening seen in the blood of the Passover, the forgiveness at Kadesh-barnea and Moses on the Mount of Transfiguration (Part 3); and finishes with the debate over losing salvation, settled through Hebrews 6 and 10 and Esau's birthright (Part 4). This course is for anyone whose assurance of salvation is shaken, or who wants to settle once and for all whether a person once saved is saved forever.

The answer was already in the Bible — 2 Corinthians 11:4: another Jesus, another spirit, another gospel. The difference comes not from the translators but from two streams of manuscripts. The oldest manuscripts read "the only begotten God," while the majority of manuscripts and the Received Text read "the only begotten Son," and both are texts the church has read. The reasoning "only begotten = born = had a beginning = a created being" collapses on three points. Monogenes means "one of a kind" (Isaac is called monogenes even though Ishmael existed, Hebrews 11:17); since the Nicene Creed the orthodox church has used "begotten, not made" as a shield against Arius; and if "only begotten" means "created," even the only begotten Son of John 3:16 falls. The problem with the Jehovah's Witnesses is not this verse but their doctrine that changes John 1:1 into "a god" and makes Christ into Michael. To the claim that "God cannot be in God," Jesus Himself gave the answer (John 14:10–11), and denying this mutual indwelling leads to tritheism. Jesus is the very exposition of God — even if our manuscripts differ, we are one family.

원수의 밭에 밀과 똑같이 생긴 독초 씨를 뿌리는 범죄가 실제로 있었고 로.en: Sowing seeds of a poisonous weed that looks just like wheat in an enemy's field was a real crime, and Roman law dealt with it. Jesus Himself interpreted this parable, and His first sentence ends our misunderstanding: "The field is the world" (Matthew 13:38). Applying this parable to problems inside the church in order to block discernment is using the text backwards. Concerning false teachers within the church, the Bible commands church discipline (Matthew 18), excommunication (1 Corinthians 5) and guarding against heretics (Titus 3:10), and the church at Ephesus was commended for testing those who called themselves apostles and exposing them as liars (Revelation 2:2). The command not to gather up the tares forbids the sword (physical removal), not the eye (discernment) — this was the very ground on which Luther opposed burning heretics. The tares, that is, darnel, cannot be told apart from wheat until the ears form; they contain a poison that makes people drunk when eaten; and at harvest, when the wheat bows its head, they stay stiff to the end — "He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck" (Proverbs 29:1). The tares do not know they are tares and serve sincerely — the "workers of iniquity (anomia)" of Matthew 7 appear again in Matthew 13:41. The lecture looks at why God waits (love for the tangled roots, and judgment that waits until the cup is full), why hardness after rebuke is judgment already begun (2 Thessalonians 2:10–11), and why a large gathering is no proof of wheat, since the tares are bound in bundles first; then it closes with the servant's four tasks: sowing, warning, testing and examining oneself. The one way not to become a tare is the humility that bows its head before rebuke.

영적분별 스토리 05 · 둘 중 하나가 데려감을 당하는 것이 휴거인가 —.en: Spiritual Discernment Story 05 · Is "One Taken, the Other Left" the Rapture? — Reading Matthew 24 Rightly (Matthew 24:29–44)

'한 사람은 데려감을 당하고 한 사람은 남겨둠을 당할 것이니라'(마 24.en: "The one shall be taken, and the other left" (Matthew 24:40) — the most famous verse used for the Rapture, yet reading it in context gives the opposite picture. Verse 29 begins "Immediately after the tribulation of those days," so verses 29–31 form one sequence after the Tribulation, and the great sound of a trumpet and the gathering from the four winds match, word for word, the restoration of Israel foretold in Isaiah 27:13 and Deuteronomy 30:4. And just before verse 40, Jesus gave the key to interpretation: in the days of Noah, those the flood took away were the wicked, and the one who remained was Noah in the ark. In Luke, to the question "Where, Lord?" the Lord answers, "Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together" (Luke 17:37) — the place they are taken is the place of judgment. The Rapture of the church was promised not on the Mount of Olives but in the upper room (John 14:2–3), and Paul unfolded it as a "mystery" (1 Corinthians 15:51). Once this distinction stands, the "Watch" of verse 42 also finds its proper place — not calculating dates but an attitude of life. Believers who hold a different view of the timing of the Rapture deserve respect, not condemnation, and the conclusion of this doctrine is "Wherefore comfort one another with these words" (1 Thessalonians 4:18).

영적분별 스토리 06 · 천사장 미가엘과 마귀는 왜 모세의 시체를 두고.en: Spiritual Discernment Story 06 · Why Did Michael the Archangel and the Devil Dispute over the Body of Moses? — Not Power but Authority (Jude 1:9)

모세가 죽고 1,400년 뒤에 기록된 유다서 1장 9절 — 천사장 미가엘.en: Jude 1:9, written some 1,400 years after Moses died, records one of the strangest scenes in the Bible: Michael the archangel and the devil disputing over the body of Moses. This lecture unpacks it with three questions. Where did this story come from? It is not recorded in Deuteronomy 34; Origen testifies that it comes from the tradition of the pseudepigraphal Assumption of Moses, but quoting a source does not make it canonical (Paul's quotations of pagan poets are a precedent). Why did the devil demand the body? True to his nature as the accuser, he accused Moses of his past killing and his disobedience at Meribah, and he schemed to make the body an instrument of idolatry. Where does "The Lord rebuke thee" come from? It quotes Zechariah 3, the LORD's verdict pronounced against Satan as he accused Joshua the high priest. After refuting the error of the Jehovah's Witnesses and similar groups who teach that Michael is Jesus — using Hebrews 1 and the absolute gap between the Son and the angels — the lecture reaches Jude's real point: the heart of spiritual warfare is not power but authority. It points out the blind spot of an aggressive spiritual warfare that imitates pronouncements of condemnation even the archangel did not make, and shows that the true weapons are submission to God and the sword of the Word. The conclusion is the Mount of Transfiguration — Moses, once accused, appeared in glory with the Lord (Matthew 17:3). Accusation cannot overturn God's final verdict.

이단으로 변질된 단체들의 충격적인 공통점 — 처음부터 악하게 시작한 곳이.en: The shocking thing that groups which turned heretical have in common is that almost none of them began as evil. Using "Having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh?" (Galatians 3:3) as a lens, this lecture dissects the four stages by which an ordinary, good church falls into a cult leader's kingdom. ① It begins not with sin but with pain (hurt) — within a pure fellowship, the seed of "only we are right" sprouts. ② "Only we are right" becomes official and walls go up — healthy criticism and orthodox theology are rejected, and the means of correction disappear. ③ The most dangerous turning point: "I alone have understood what no one knew for 2,000 years" — one man's interpretation rises above the Bible. ④ Amid the applause of believers who have stopped pushing back, a leader no one can restrain is born. The lecture offers three biblical standards for discerning such a leader — titles and deification that leave behind the place of a brother; a family kept behind a veil, or a pastor's wife overstepping her role behind the scenes (Jezebel, 1 Kings 21); and the practice of branding believers who call for purification as traitors and driving them out — and with compassion explains why people inside cannot get out on their own (deception disguised as an angel of light, and self-defense over the years they have given, 2 Corinthians 11:14). Discern not by the clothing but by the fruit (Matthew 7:16) — above all, the testimony of those who left wounded is the most honest report card. These four stages are not about one particular group but are seeds in every community; a church where questions are still alive is a healthy church.

성경에서 가장 기이한 기적 하나 — 모압 약탈대에 쫓겨 급히 던져진 시체.en: One of the strangest miracles in the Bible: a body, hastily thrown down as a band of Moabite raiders approached, touched the bones of Elisha, revived and stood up on its feet (2 Kings 13:21). Did Elisha come back to life? Was there power in the bones? If so, should we venerate relics? The lecture answers with three readings. ① Reading the subject rightly — the one who came back to life was not Elisha but the man who was thrown in. ② Reading the background — northern Israel weakened under Syrian oppression, Moabite bands that invaded every year, and cave tombs where a body could be laid just by opening a stone door explain the urgency of the scene. ③ Reading the context — it pairs with the deathbed prophecy in the paragraph just before ("thou shalt smite Syria but thrice," 2 Kings 13:14–19). It was a sign confirming that though the prophet was dead, the word from his mouth was alive, and the prophecy was fulfilled exactly (13:25). Three biblical objections stand against relic veneration: the silence of Scripture, in which no one ever sought out those bones; the way the Bible records even miracles through objects as coming from God (Acts 19:11); and the precedent of the brasen serpent, which had become an object of worship and was broken in pieces and called "Nehushtan" (2 Kings 18:4). When the channel is mistaken for the source, faith turns into magic. This event points further on: Elisha, who gave life to another yet stayed in the grave, is the shadow; Christ, who rose by His own power and became the firstfruits (1 Corinthians 15:20), is the substance. And beside that miracle stands one verse — God, remembering His covenant, would not destroy them (2 Kings 13:23). Even in places that seem dead, the promise of restoration still stands.

창세기 5장 선조들의 수명 통계 데이터를 바탕으로 한 천년왕국 수명 회복.en: How realistic is restored lifespan in the Millennium? Looking at the lifespans of the patriarchs in Genesis 5

노아의 홍수 및 벨렉 시대 이후 인간 수명이 급감하는 생물학적 지수 감세.en: Analyzing the exponential-decay pattern of human lifespan after Noah's Flood and the days of Peleg

대홍수 이후 인간의 수명이 꺾이게 된 3가지 핵심 원인 (환경 격변, 유.en: 3 key reasons human lifespan dropped after the Flood (environmental upheaval, genetic entropy, the working of the curse)

이사야 65장 20절에 기록된 '100세의 어린이' 구절이 가진 성경적.en: The true biblical meaning of restoration in Isaiah 65:20's "the child shall die an hundred years old"

현대 노화 의학 학회의 최신 연구 기준과 성경 속 노화 조절 프로그램 메.en: Current findings in aging research and how they line up with the Bible's picture of a regulated lifespan

천년왕국 시대에 인간의 장수와 질병 치유를 가능하게 만드는 3가지 복합적.en: 3 combined factors that make long life and healing possible in the Millennial age

천년왕국 시기 예외적으로 적용되는 죽음의 성격과 영원한 나라에서의 완전한.en: The exceptional nature of death in the Millennium, and death abolished completely in the eternal kingdom

천년왕국의 폭발적인 인구 증가 법칙 추정 및 사막 변화를 통한 지구 부양.en: Estimating explosive population growth in the Millennium, and the earth's capacity restored as deserts bloom

수백 년의 세대를 아우르는 가정이루기와 첫째 부활에 참여한 성도들의 완전.en: Families spanning centuries of generations, and first-resurrection saints as perfect teachers

완벽한 환경과 교육 시스템 속에서도 사탄의 미혹을 택하는 현상을 통해 본.en: Human sinfulness laid bare: people choosing Satan's deception even with a perfect environment and education

오늘을 살아가는 성도 인생의 가치와 마지막 때 복음 전파 및 그리스도 대.en: The worth of a believer's life today, and the charge to preach the gospel as Christ's ambassadors in the last days

20분 특강 · 짐승의 표 666의 실체.en: 20-Minute Special Lecture · The Truth About 666, the Mark of the Beast

베리칩, 바코드, 백신까지 — 끝없이 반복되는 666 괴담, 무엇이 진실.en: VeriChip, barcodes, even vaccines — the 666 rumors never stop coming back, but what is the truth? Working from the text of Revelation — from the meaning of the original word for "the mark of the beast" (charagma), through answers to five historical misunderstandings, to the four essentials of the mark — this lecture gives you a standard of discernment so that you are no longer shaken by conspiracy theories.

'짐승의 표(카라그마)' 원어의 진짜 의미.en: The real meaning of the original word for "the mark of the beast" (charagma)

666 숫자의 성경적 해석 (게마트리아).en: A biblical interpretation of the number 666 (gematria)

오해와 반박 ① 네로 황제.en: Misunderstanding and answer ① Emperor Nero

오해와 반박 ② 로마 교황.en: Misunderstanding and answer ② The Roman pope

오해와 반박 ③ 베리칩(RFID).en: Misunderstanding and answer ③ The VeriChip (RFID)

마지막 시대를 살아가는 성도의 자세.en: The posture of believers living in the last days

천년왕국 스토리 10 · 사해에서 낚시를? 가짜뉴스인가?.en: Millennium Story 10 · Fishing in the Dead Sea? Is It Fake News?

천년왕국이 되면 죽음의 바다 사해에서 물고기를 낚는다는 예언, 과연 가짜.en: When the Millennium comes, will people really catch fish in the Dead Sea, the sea of death — or is that prophecy fake news? Step by step, this lecture looks through Bible prophecy at the land that will be restored and the great upheaval of the earth's environment.

천년왕국 스토리 11 · 세 사람은 원래 한가족, 이들의 운명은?.en: Millennium Story 11 · Three Peoples Who Were Once One Family — What Is Their Destiny?

천년왕국에서 사람들의 신분과 역할은 어떻게 나뉠까요? 원래 한 가족에서.en: How will people's status and roles be divided in the Millennium? From the Bible, and from the standpoint of Israel, the church and the nations, this lecture unpacks the different destinies of three groups who branched off from what was once a single family.

천년왕국 스토리 12 · SF가 아니다! 하늘에서 내려오는 새 예루살렘,.en: Millennium Story 12 · This Is Not Science Fiction! The New Jerusalem Coming Down from Heaven — the Truth About a 2,200 km City in the Sky

하늘에서 내려오는 새 예루살렘 성을 SF가 아닌 성경의 약속으로 살펴봅니.en: This lecture looks at the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from heaven — not as science fiction but as a promise of the Bible. It explains the size of a city that measures some 2,200 km and who will enter into it.

천년왕국 스토리 13 · 동물의 희생제사를 왜 다시? 에스겔 성전의 모든.en: Millennium Story 13 · Why Animal Sacrifices Again? Everything About Ezekiel's Temple

천년왕국 때 에스겔 성전에서 동물 희생제사가 다시 드려진다는 예언의 의미.en: This lecture examines the meaning of the prophecy that animal sacrifices will again be offered in Ezekiel's temple during the Millennium. From the Bible, it explains sacrifices offered as remembrance and worship — something of an entirely different order from the atonement completed once for all on the cross.

천년왕국 스토리 14 · 자본주의도 공산주의도 다 틀렸다! 제3의 체제.en: Millennium Story 14 · Capitalism and Communism Are Both Wrong! The Third System

인류가 세운 자본주의도 공산주의도 답이 되지 못한 이유와, 그리스도께서.en: From Bible prophecy, this lecture explains why neither capitalism nor communism — the systems mankind has built — could be the answer, and unfolds the "third system": the Millennial Kingdom ruled by Christ Himself.

천년왕국 스토리 15 · 유대인의 마지막 절기 장막절의 비밀.en: Millennium Story 15 · The Secret of the Feast of Tabernacles, the Last of Israel's Feasts

이스라엘의 일곱 절기 가운데 오직 초막절(장막절)만이 천년왕국 시대까지.en: From the Bible, this lecture explains why, of Israel's seven feasts, only the Feast of Tabernacles (Booths) will still be kept in the Millennial age. In an age that has lost what it means to be "together," it sheds light on the high point of Immanuel — God dwelling with His people.

천년왕국 스토리 16 · 어린양의 혼인잔치의 모든 것.en: Millennium Story 16 · Everything About the Marriage Supper of the Lamb

어린양의 혼인잔치가 무엇이며 재림과 천년왕국에서 어떻게 성취되는지 성경으.en: From the Bible, this lecture explains what the marriage supper of the Lamb is and how it is fulfilled at the Second Coming and in the Millennium.

천년왕국 스토리 17 · 지금도 새로운 계시(꿈·환상·예언)가 있는가?.en: Millennium Story 17 · Are There Still New Revelations Today (Dreams, Visions, Prophecies)?

요엘 2:28 \"내 영을 부어 주리라\"를 근거로 오늘날에도 새 계시가.en: Some claim on the basis of Joel 2:28, "I will pour out my spirit," that new revelations are still given today. This lecture tests that claim in the light of the context of Joel and Acts 2.

천년왕국 스토리 18 · 곡과 마곡 1차 전쟁과 재림 때 어린양의 혼인.en: Millennium Story 18 · The First War of Gog and Magog, and Preparing the Marriage Supper of the Lamb at the Second Coming (Ezekiel 39)

에스겔 38~39장 곡과 마곡 1차 전쟁과 요한계시록 20장의 2차 전쟁.en: This lecture distinguishes the first war of Gog and Magog in Ezekiel 38–39 from the second war in Revelation 20, and shows that the marriage supper of the Millennium begins on a cleansed land, once the weapons have been burned and the dead have been buried.

천년왕국 스토리 19 · 곡과 마곡 1차 전쟁 심화편 — 러시아·이란 연.en: Millennium Story 19 · The First War of Gog and Magog, In Depth — Russia and Iran's Coalition vs. Israel (Ezekiel 38)

에스겔 38장 곡의 침략 연합군(로스·메섹·두발·바사·구스·붓 등)의 정.en: An in-depth study of who makes up Gog's invading coalition in Ezekiel 38 (Rosh, Meshech, Tubal, Persia, Ethiopia, Libya and others), looking at it against today's picture of the far north, Russia and Iran, and explaining how this first war of Gog and Magog becomes the prelude to the end. Rather than hastily pinning it on particular nations or events, it discerns humbly within the framework of the text.

천년왕국 스토리 20 · 사탄의 광기가 쏟아지는 아마겟돈 전쟁 — 왜 이.en: Millennium Story 20 · The Battle of Armageddon, Where Satan's Fury Pours Out — Why This War Is Inevitable

일곱 인·나팔·대접의 심판으로 초토화된 대환난 끝물, 폐허 위에서 인류.en: At the tail end of the Great Tribulation, with the earth laid waste by the seven seal, trumpet and bowl judgments, the largest war in human history — the Battle of Armageddon — breaks out on the ruins. From the Bible, this lecture explains why this war must happen, as three necessities converge — Satan's, mankind's and God's — along with the meaning of the overflowing blood and the cleanup that follows, and the marriage supper of the Lamb that will begin on a cleansed land.

천년왕국 스토리 21 · 인류 최후의 전쟁 — 곡과 마곡 2차 전쟁(요한.en: Millennium Story 21 · Mankind's Final War — The Second War of Gog and Magog (Revelation 20)

천년왕국 끝, 사탄이 잠깐 놓여 바다의 모래 같은 무리를 미혹해 일으키는.en: At the end of the Millennium, Satan is loosed for a little season and deceives a multitude as the sand of the sea, stirring up mankind's final war. Why would a generation raised in a perfect environment rise up against God? This lecture shows that the source of sin is not the environment but the human heart, and that salvation is new birth from beginning to end.

특강 · 마지막 때 세 전쟁 총정리 — 곡과 마곡 1차 · 아마겟돈 ·.en: Special Lecture · The Three Wars of the Last Days, Summed Up — First Gog and Magog · Armageddon · Second Gog and Magog

마지막 때 인류가 겪을 세 전쟁을 한 번에 정리한 90분 통합 특강입니다.en: A 90-minute combined special lecture that covers the three wars mankind will face in the last days all at once. It distinguishes the first war of Gog and Magog at the start of the Great Tribulation (Ezekiel 38–39), Armageddon at the end of the Tribulation, and the second war of Gog and Magog at the end of the Millennium (Revelation 20) by their timing, scale and outcome, so you can grasp the timeline of the end at a glance.

천년왕국 스토리 22 · 바깥 어두운 데서 슬피 울며 이를 갈리라 — 구.en: Millennium Story 22 · "Cast Out into Outer Darkness: There Shall Be Weeping and Gnashing of Teeth" — Loss of Salvation, or Salvation by Works?

‘바깥 어두운 데 쫓겨나 슬피 울며 이를 갈리라’를 구원 취소의 협박이나.en: This lecture tests against Scripture the interpretation that uses "cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth" as a threat of losing one's salvation or as pressure toward loyalty and service. It opens all seven places where this expression is used to identify the place and the people in view, and it brings to light the wedding garment at the marriage feast, the focus of the parable of the talents, and who it is that is "without" the city in Revelation.

천년왕국 스토리 23 · 마병대 2억이 인류 3분의 1을 죽인다 — 에스.en: Millennium Story 23 · An Army of 200 Million Horsemen Kills a Third of Mankind — The War of Ezekiel 38 vs. the Plague of Revelation 9

에스겔 38장의 곡과 마곡 1차 전쟁과 계시록 9장 여섯째 나팔의 2억.en: This lecture contrasts the first war of Gog and Magog in Ezekiel 38 with the plague of the 200-million-strong army of horsemen at the sixth trumpet in Revelation 9 on seven points — direction of invasion, target, agents, weapons, the way God intervenes, outcome and timing — and shows that they are separate events. Revelation 9 is not a war between nations but a judgment carried out by God.

천년왕국 스토리 24 · 사람의 영혼까지 상품이 된다 — 두 바벨론의 신.en: Millennium Story 24 · Even the Souls of Men Become Merchandise — The Mystery and Fate of the Two Babylons

계시록 17장의 바벨론(이마에 신비가 붙은 종교적 실체)과 18장의 바벨.en: This lecture distinguishes the Babylon of Revelation 17 (a religious entity with "Mystery" written on her forehead) from the Babylon of Revelation 18 (the great city, commercial and political, with the mystery gone). It follows what is meant by the "souls of men" placed at the end of the list of merchandise, the collapse in one hour, and the Battle of Armageddon and the Lord's return to the earth that follow.

천년왕국 스토리 25 · 성령 훼방죄의 모든 것 — 오는 세상에서도 용서.en: Millennium Story 25 · Everything About Blasphemy Against the Holy Spirit — A Sin Not Forgiven Even in the World to Come?

마태복음 12장의 현장으로 들어가 성령 훼방죄가 충분한 빛과 고의성과 완.en: Stepping into the scene of Matthew 12, this lecture shows that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit concerns a case where full light, deliberate intent and stubborn hardness are all present together, and it contrasts this with the restoration of Peter and Paul. From Scripture it refutes the way this verse is misused today — to forbid any criticism of pastors, to shut down any testing of a ministry, and to block questions about finances. It confirms that "the world to come" is not purgatory but the messianic kingdom, and it closes with comfort for fearful believers: that very fear is itself a sign of the Holy Spirit at work.

천년왕국 스토리 26 · 침례자 요한, 여자가 낳은 자 중에 가장 큰 자.en: Millennium Story 26 · John the Baptist, the Greatest Among Those Born of Women — Who Is the Bride of the Lamb?

가장 큰 자로 불린 침례자 요한이 스스로를 신랑의 친구라 고백한 이유를.en: Following why John the Baptist, called the greatest, confessed himself to be the friend of the Bridegroom, this lecture brings to light the order of the resurrection (the tagma of 1 Corinthians 15 and the harvest feasts of Leviticus 23), the timing of the resurrection of Old Testament saints and Tribulation martyrs, the 75-day transition period that comes from the 1,290 days and the 1,335 days, and the key point that the qualification of the bride is set by the manner of union.

천년왕국 스토리 27 · 구원받는 숫자가 14만 4천 명? — 이단이 악.en: Millennium Story 27 · Only 144,000 Will Be Saved? — Reading Revelation 7 Rightly, a Chapter Cults Abuse

이단에 빠진 자녀의 사연에서 출발해, 구원의 정원이 14만 4천으로 정해.en: Starting from the story of a family whose child was drawn into a cult, this lecture dissects the three-step mechanism by which the doctrine that the number of the saved is fixed at 144,000 traps people. Revelation 7:4–8 itself identifies them as the twelve tribes of Israel, and just five verses later, verse 9 shows a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations and kindreds — so the doctrine of a fixed quota collapses within the very same passage. It also covers the timing and purpose of the sealing, the evangelistic ministry of the Great Tribulation and the firstfruits on Mount Zion, the standing of church-age believers, and three questions for discerning a cult.

천년왕국 스토리 28 · “환난에서 나오는 자들” — 이 헬라어가 휴거를.en: Millennium Story 28 · "They Which Came Out of Great Tribulation" — Does This Greek Phrase Overturn the Rapture?

환난 통과설이 근거로 드는 세 구절을 원어와 문맥으로 검토한다. 요한계시.en: This lecture examines, in the original language and in context, three verses that the posttribulation view relies on. In Revelation 7:14, the preposition ek, the double article and the present participle clearly point to a multitude that goes through the Tribulation — but there is no basis for assuming that this multitude is the church. The scene in which the elder asks John who they are, and the structure in which the church disappears from the earth after chapter 4, point the other way. In Matthew 24:22, "no flesh" refers not to the salvation of the soul but to physical survival, and "the elect" also follow the context of Judea. The debate over the timing of the two witnesses is no obstacle to understanding chapter 7, an interlude vision. The conclusion: be sharp in discernment and gentle in attitude.

천년왕국 스토리 29 · 십사만 사천, 환난 성도, 어린양의 신부의 정체.en: Millennium Story 29 · The 144,000, the Tribulation Saints and the Bride of the Lamb — Revelation 14:1–5

7장에서 인 맞은 십사만 사천이 칠 년 환난을 다 통과하고도 한 사람도.en: It begins with the roll call of chapter 14: the 144,000 sealed in chapter 7 have passed through the whole seven-year Tribulation and stand on Mount Zion without losing a single one. The lecture then unfolds, in turn, the providence of the remnant that runs from Noah's household of eight to the seven thousand of Elijah's day; the design of 12 × 12 × 1,000, the same as the New Jerusalem; the sealing as a stamp of ownership, and its counterfeit, the mark of the beast; the firstfruits that pledge the harvest of the whole field; and the Lamb on Mount Zion who answers the question asked on Mount Moriah. Finally, it distinguishes the three groups of the Millennium: the 144,000 as a kingdom of priests, the bride of the Lamb who will reign as kings, and the Tribulation saints as guests at the marriage supper.

천년왕국 스토리 30 · 영원한 복음은 다른 복음인가 — 세 천사의 선포.en: Millennium Story 30 · Is the Everlasting Gospel a Different Gospel? — Five Question Marks in the Proclamation of the Three Angels

요한계시록 14장 6~13절 여덟 절에 박힌 다섯 개의 물음표를 차례로.en: One by one, this lecture pulls out the five question marks lodged in the eight verses of Revelation 14:6–13. It establishes that the adjective "everlasting" points not to a new gospel but to the one and only gospel, foretold in Eden and fulfilled at the cross, and it reads the prophetic perfect — which announces a Babylon not yet fallen as already fallen — side by side with Romans 8:30. It explains the undiluted wine of wrath, and the torment received in the presence of the Lamb, in the light of the cup of Gethsemane, and it tests the reading that turns "they that keep the commandments of God" into a command to keep the Sabbath in four steps: the argument from absence, what the mark really is, the error of tense, and the plumb line of Galatians. Finally, it shows the exchange of rest, as "they have no rest" in verse 11 and "that they may rest" in verse 13 interlock as words of the same family.

천년왕국 스토리 31 · 마지막 때 추수는 왜 두 번인가 — 알곡의 낫과.en: Millennium Story 31 · Why Are There Two Harvests in the Last Days? — The Sickle of the Grain and the Winepress of Wrath

요한계시록 14장 14~20절의 두 추수를 낫을 든 주체와 거두어지는 대.en: This lecture reads the two harvests of Revelation 14:14–20 along three lines: who holds the sickle, what is gathered in, and the vocabulary the text uses. In the first scene, where one like unto the Son of man on a white cloud reaps the grain, there is no wrath, no fire and no blood; in the second, where an angel who came out from the altar gathers the clusters of the vine of the earth, the great winepress of the wrath of God, blood reaching to the horse bridles and sixteen hundred furlongs are packed into four verses. Setting side by side, with their reasons, the view that reads both harvests as judgment and the view that reads them as salvation and judgment, it then sets out three settled points that stand firm whichever view one takes. Finally, it explains from the longsuffering of God in Genesis 15:16 why the cry "How long, O Lord" of Revelation 6:10 has been held back until now, and shows how the name Gethsemane — meaning "oil press" — turns this fearful passage into an invitation.

천년왕국 스토리 32 · 30분 총정리(상) — 천년왕국은 왜 새 하늘.en: Millennium Story 32 · 30-Minute Review (Part 1) — Why the Millennium Is Not the New Heaven and New Earth

천년왕국 세미나 전체를 개막·통치·결말의 삼막으로 압축한 총정리 상편이다.en: The first half of the series review, condensing the whole Millennium Seminar into three acts: the opening, the reign and the conclusion. First, it divides the Millennium of Revelation 20 from the new heaven and new earth of Revelation 21–22 by four criteria — the setting, the time, the people and the state of sin — making clear that one is the restoration of this earth and the other a new creation. It then reviews the return of the King on the white horse, the binding of Satan with its words "he must be loosed a little season," the judgment of the sheep and the goats, and the first resurrection completed in three ranks, and confirms from Isaiah the reign with Jerusalem as its capital and the daily life of a people in natural bodies. Finally, it explains why that blessed kingdom still needs death and a rule with a rod of iron, and how the rebellion at the end of the thousand years — a multitude as the sand of the sea following Satan when he is loosed — settles that mankind's problem is not the environment but the heart. The Great White Throne judgment and the new heaven and new earth are covered in Part 2.

천년왕국 스토리 33 · 총정리(하) — 백보좌 심판과 새 하늘 새 땅.en: Millennium Story 33 · Review (Part 2) — The Great White Throne Judgment and the New Heaven and New Earth

33편에 걸친 천년왕국 시리즈를 닫는 마지막 강의이자 총정리 하편이다..en: The final lecture closing the 33-part Millennium series, and the second half of the review. It dissects the court of the great white throne — standing alone where the earth and the heaven have fled away — in four elements: judge, defendants, evidence and verdict. As it is written that the Father "hath committed all judgment unto the Son," the judge is Jesus Christ, seated as the righteous Judge, and the defendants are the dead of the second resurrection, given up by the sea, by death and by hell. It unpacks the two-part structure of this court — the books recording works determine the fairness of the judgment and the degree of punishment, while the Lamb's book of life decides between heaven and the lake of fire — and shows why the second death, in which even death and hell are cast into the lake of fire, is not annihilation. It then sets out how believers in natural bodies are changed into resurrection bodies without seeing death, and the five features of the new heaven and new earth created after the old has been dismantled down to its very elements — a kingdom with no sea, no temple, no sun or moon and no night, where the curse and death are ended and God Himself wipes away the tears. Standing before the beginning of eternity beyond the completion of history, it asks whether your name is written in the book of life.

특강 · 50분에 끝내는 천년왕국 — 총정리 상·하 통합.en: Special Lecture · The Millennium in 50 Minutes — Review Parts 1 & 2 Combined

천년왕국 스토리 32(총정리 상)와 33(총정리 하)을 한 편으로 묶은.en: A combined special lecture that brings Millennium Story 32 (Review, Part 1) and 33 (Review, Part 2) together into one. It condenses the whole Millennium into three acts — the opening, the reign and the conclusion — sets out the four criteria that separate the Millennium from the new heaven and new earth, and then covers the four elements of the Great White Throne judgment and the second death, the change of believers in natural bodies, and the five features of the new heaven and new earth, completing the full map of the series in about 50 minutes. If you don't have time to watch both parts separately, this one lecture is enough.

특강 · 80분에 끝내는 요한계시록 14장 — 십사만 사천 · 세 천사의.en: Special Lecture · Revelation 14 in 80 Minutes — The 144,000 · The Three Angels' Proclamation · The Two Harvests, Summed Up

천년왕국 스토리 29·30·31에서 나눈 요한계시록 14장 전체를 한 편.en: An 80-minute combined special lecture that brings together all of Revelation 14, which was covered across Millennium Story 29, 30 and 31. In order, it covers who the 144,000 standing on Mount Zion are (vv. 1–5); the proclamation of the three angels concerning the everlasting gospel, the prophetic perfect of Babylon's fall and the mark of the beast (vv. 6–13); and the two harvests divided into the sickle of the grain and the winepress of wrath (vv. 14–20). From the text itself it refutes the cult claim that reads the 144,000 as its own group, as well as the interpretation that makes verse 12 the basis for Sabbath doctrine, and it shows why Revelation 14 is a preview of the Millennium placed in the midst of the despair of chapter 13.

풀버전 1 · 천년왕국 세미나 1~9강 몰아보기 — 왜 천국 전에 천년왕.en: Full Version 1 · Millennium Seminar Lectures 1–9 Back to Back — Why the Millennium Comes Before Heaven

천년왕국 세미나 1강부터 9강까지를 끊지 않고 이어 붙인 다섯 시간짜리.en: A five-hour full-version marathon that joins Lectures 1 through 9 of the Millennium Seminar without a break. Starting from the framework that the Millennium is a real kingdom — the last chapter of the restoration of kingship, in which the second Adam takes back the dominion the first Adam lost (Lecture 1) — it passes in one breath up nine steps: four ways of reading the thousand years (Lecture 2); the five-stage timeline of the church age → the seven-year Great Tribulation → the Millennium → Satan's final rebellion → the eternal kingdom (Lecture 3); the last of Daniel 9's seventy weeks and the pretribulation Rapture (Lecture 4); Armageddon, a script written by God (Lecture 5); the first resurrection completed in three ranks (Lecture 6); the sheep and the goats as a real judgment (Lecture 7); a Millennium with no automatic salvation (Lecture 8); and sin that remains even with 900-year lifespans (Lecture 9). Because it is an introductory course built in order, it is an ideal first guide for anyone who has wondered about the end times but didn't know where to start.

풀버전 2 · 천년왕국 세미나 10~19강 몰아보기 — 회복된 땅에서 마.en: Full Version 2 · Millennium Seminar Lectures 10–19 Back to Back — From the Restored Earth to the Final Test

천년왕국 세미나 10강부터 19강까지를 한 편으로 이어 붙인 다섯 시간짜.en: A five-hour full-version marathon that joins Lectures 10 through 19 of the Millennium Seminar into one. If Lectures 1–9 built the framework, this part fills in what actually happens within that kingdom. It walks up ten steps: the Mount of Olives split in two and the Dead Sea brought back to life (Lecture 10); family, status and the cultural mandate (Lecture 11); the New Jerusalem, a 2,200 km cube in which the Holy of Holies is enlarged (Lecture 12); Ezekiel's temple, with memorial sacrifices that impress the cross on the heart (Lecture 13); a third system, a theocracy that is neither capitalism nor communism (Lecture 14); why, of the seven feasts, only the Feast of Tabernacles remains (Lecture 15); the wedding in heaven and the marriage supper on earth (Lecture 16); when Joel 2:28 is finally fulfilled (Lecture 17); and the first war of Gog and Magog with its in-depth sequel, which separates two wars that share one name (Lectures 18 and 19). Why, in so perfect a kingdom, must Satan be "loosed a little season"? It moves toward the conclusion that mankind's problem is not the environment but the heart.

풀버전 3 · 천년왕국 세미나 20~33강 몰아보기 — 아마겟돈에서 새.en: Full Version 3 · Millennium Seminar Lectures 20–33 Back to Back — From Armageddon to the New Heaven and New Earth

천년왕국 세미나 20강부터 33강까지를 한 편으로 이어 붙인 여섯 시간.en: The third full-version marathon, six and a half hours long, joining Lectures 20 through 33 of the Millennium Seminar into one. It begins with Armageddon, where the necessities of Satan, mankind and God converge (Lecture 20), and moves on through the second war of Gog and Magog, when Satan is loosed for a little season after the thousand years are expired (Lecture 21); "outer darkness," which means neither loss of salvation nor salvation by works (Lecture 22); the war of Ezekiel 38 and the plague of Revelation 9, which resemble each other only in scale (Lecture 23); two Babylons that share only a name (Lecture 24); the three conditions of blasphemy against the Holy Spirit (Lecture 25); John the Baptist, the friend of the Bridegroom, and the bride of the Lamb (Lecture 26); the places of the 144,000, the Tribulation saints and the church (Lectures 27–29); the everlasting gospel, which is no different gospel (Lecture 30); and the sickle of the grain and the winepress of wrath (Lecture 31). It ties the series together with why the Millennium is not the new heaven and new earth (Lecture 32) and what decides eternity at the Great White Throne judgment (Lecture 33). Two wars, two Babylons, two harvests, two resurrections, two deaths — yet only one book of life: that is the conclusion it races toward.

북콘서트 사전질문 01 · 예수님 때 살아난 성도들도 첫째 부활인가 —.en: Book Concert Pre-Questions 01 · Were the Saints Raised at Jesus' Resurrection Part of the First Resurrection? — Resuscitation vs. Resurrection

「천년왕국을 아십니까」 북콘서트 사전 질문 문답 1편. 예수님 부활 때.en: Part 1 of the Q&A on questions sent in ahead of the book concert for "Do You Know the Millennium?" Did the saints who rose from their graves at Jesus' resurrection (Matthew 27:52–53) die again later, and are they also part of the first resurrection? Starting with how to hold back from speculation where the Bible is silent, it separates resuscitation from resurrection by what the seven people who died and were brought back to life have in common (all of them died again) and by the definition of resurrection that Jesus Himself gave — "Neither can they die any more" (Luke 20:35–36). Then, by way of the ordinance in Leviticus 23 that the firstfruits were not a single grain but a sheaf, and the "every man in his own order" (tagma) of 1 Corinthians 15:23, it lays out the procession of the first resurrection — Christ and the sheaf of firstfruits, then the church, then the Old Testament saints and Tribulation martyrs — and even explains why a "midtribulation rapture" is not found in the Bible.

북콘서트 사전질문 02 · 새 하늘 새 땅에서는 다 똑같아지는가 — 본성.en: Book Concert Pre-Questions 02 · Will Everyone Be the Same in the New Heaven and New Earth? — Nature and Office: The Same Life, a Different Glory

사전 질문 문답 2편. 천년왕국을 자연인의 몸으로 통과한 백성도 새 예루.en: Part 2 of the pre-submitted Q&A. Will those who passed through the Millennium in natural bodies also be glorified when they enter the New Jerusalem — and if so, will they become just like the resurrected saints who reigned, so that the distinction of ruling disappears? Laying "flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God" (1 Corinthians 15:50) over "there shall be no more death" (Revelation 21:4), it first establishes the change of the people in natural bodies, and then answers the heart of the question by distinguishing nature from office. The nature of the body becomes the same, but just as "one star differeth from another star in glory" (1 Corinthians 15:41), glory remains distinct forever; even in the eternal city there are nations, kings and a reign for ever and ever (Revelation 21:24; 22:5); and the place of the bride of the Lamb is a relationship that belongs to the church alone. With the picture of a diploma (the body) and a position (the office), it completes the idea of "the same life, a different glory."

북콘서트 사전질문 03 · 환난 성도는 행위로 구원받는가 — 증거와 원인.en: Book Concert Pre-Questions 03 · Are Tribulation Saints Saved by Works? — Evidence vs. Cause, Series Finale

사전 질문 문답 완결편. 교회가 휴거된 뒤 환난기에는 행위로 구원받는다는.en: The final part of the pre-submitted Q&A. Is it true that after the church is raptured, people in the Tribulation will be saved by works? The conclusion first: in no age is there salvation by works. Starting from "lest any man should boast" (Ephesians 2:8–9) and going on to the Tribulation saints who washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb (Revelation 7:14), it establishes that the ground of salvation (the blood) and its means (faith) are the same in every age, and that only the amount of revelation changes. It then dissects three passages that have been read as salvation by works: the parable of the ten virgins is a warning against a false profession without oil (the Holy Spirit, the reality); the salvation of "he that shall endure unto the end" is physical survival, as verse 22 of the same chapter makes clear; and the good deeds of the sheep among the sheep and goats are evidence of faith, done "in the name of a disciple" (Matthew 10:42). It answers the worry about pride with "what hast thou that thou didst not receive?" (1 Corinthians 4:7), and binds all three parts together with three pairs of keys: resuscitation and resurrection, nature and office, evidence and cause.

요한계시록 13장 ④ · 짐승의 표, 모르고 받을 수 있을까 — 다섯 가.en: Revelation 13 ④ · The Mark of the Beast: Could You Take It Without Knowing? — Five Misunderstandings, Summed Up

바코드·베리칩·백신이 차례로 666으로 지목됐다 빗나간 역사에서 출발해.en: Starting from the history of barcodes, the VeriChip and vaccines each being named as 666 in turn and each missing the mark, this lecture clears up five misunderstandings. The mark goes hand in hand with worship, so no one can receive it unknowingly (Revelation 14:9); its essence is not a machine but a seal of allegiance (charagma); and 666 is not a calculation but "the number of a man who tries to become God yet never reaches 7." Believers have already received a different mark: the sealing of the Holy Spirit (Ephesians 1:13).

히말라야에서 폭 610미터의 얼음과 바위가 1,200미터 아래로 무너져.en: This lecture reads through the eyes of the Bible the disaster in the Himalayas, in which a mass of ice and rock 610 meters wide plunged 1,200 meters and set off an inland tsunami. First, it asks whether this disaster was a punishment aimed at its victims, and answers from Luke 13, where Jesus twice says "Nay" — showing that disaster is not a condemnation of the dead but a loudspeaker calling the living to repentance. Second, it explains the reality of a crumbling creation through the vanity and the bondage of corruption described in Romans 8, and points out that this pain is not death but the pains of childbirth — the travail toward a new creation. Third, it turns to the second and third trumpets of Revelation 8, making clear that this disaster is not the fulfillment of the trumpet judgments but a foreshadowing of them, and it closes with this conclusion: do not count the days — discern the season.

Just as a 40,000-piece puzzle needs the picture on the box lid, this book needs a map. Jesus, its Author, personally gave a three-part table of contents in Revelation 1:19: “the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter.” The things seen are the glorified Christ of chapter 1; the things which are, the seven churches of chapters 2–3, that is, the church age; the things hereafter, all of chapters 4–22. On top of this we lay a full map subdivided into the heavenly throne (chapters 4–5), the seven-year Tribulation and the Second Coming (6–19), the Millennium and the great white throne (20), and the new heaven and new earth (21–22). We observe that “church,” which appears nineteen times in chapters 2–3, never appears on earth after 4:1, and we read the “after this” (meta tauta) and “Come up hither” of 4:1 together with 1 Thessalonians 4. Finally, setting Genesis 1–3 beside Revelation 20–22, we see that the Bible is one book whose beginning and end fit together, and that we now stand between the close of chapter 3 and 4:1.

This lecture lays the seven misconceptions that have sealed up Revelation on the operating table of the Word and untangles them one by one (it is a frightening book; it cannot be interpreted; finding the person who is 666; never think about timing; the church too will pass through the Tribulation; it has all been fulfilled already; the Millennium is only a figure of speech), and then offers a practical test for weighing views: does it awaken a sense of imminence, or dull it?

기초 과정을 마치고 본문을 한 절씩 강해하기 시작하는 첫 강의입니다. 흘.en: This is the first lecture to expound the text verse by verse after the foundation course. Three verses of greeting that are easy to skim were in fact a declaration against an empire. “The prince of the kings of the earth” was a title of the emperor; the emperor alone was both king and high priest; and “who was, and is, and shall be” was a hymn offered to Zeus. John changes that last word to “is to come.” In verse 4 we look at an expression that breaks Greek grammar (ho ēn) so as not to attach a “beginning” to God, three reasons the seven Spirits before the throne are the Holy Spirit, and how the order Father · Spirit · Son is the order of the heavenly throne John saw. In verse 5 we show that Jesus’ three titles come from Psalm 89, the psalm of the Davidic covenant, and reveal in turn the three offices of prophet, priest and king, and why “the first begotten” does not mean “the first created.” In verse 6 we trace how the conditional offer at Sinai, “if ye will … keep my covenant, ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests,” became the completed “hath made us” through the blood of Christ, and reach the conclusion: the saints are priests now, and will be kings hereafter.

요한계시록 스토리 06 · 재림 때 사람들은 왜 통곡하는가 — 구름 타고.en: Revelation Story 06 · Why Will People Wail at the Second Coming? — He Who Comes with Clouds, Alpha and Omega, Write It in a Book and Send It (Rev 1:7–11)

1장 7절 한 절에 다니엘 7장 13절(구름 타고 오심)과 스가랴 12장.en: The single verse Revelation 1:7 combines Daniel 7:13 (coming with clouds) and Zechariah 12:10 (they that pierced him shall look and mourn), and Jesus himself made that combination first in Matthew 24:30. Three things follow. The Second Coming is a visible event that every eye will see, so an invisible presence, a spiritual coming, or a fulfillment in AD 70 has no ground to stand on; the mourning of “they also which pierced him” is the mourning of repentance that leads into Zechariah 13:1; and this scene is not the Rapture in the air but the Second Coming to the earth that the whole world will see. Alpha and Omega and the Almighty in verse 8, and “the first and the last” in verse 11, are the very names the LORD claimed for himself alone in Isaiah 44:6 (“beside me there is no God”), now given to Jesus — the Christology of Revelation. The lecture goes on to the Christian life summed up by an apostle past ninety who calls himself “your brother” — tribulation, kingdom and patience; “the Lord’s day,” which can be read both as Sunday and as the end-time “day of the LORD”; the nature of written revelation in the command “write in a book, and send it”; and the seven churches, arranged in the order of the Roman road, read as a blueprint of the church age.

요한계시록 스토리 07 · 재림 때 예수님의 모습은 상상을 초월한다 —.en: Revelation Story 07 · Jesus at His Coming Is Beyond Imagination — The High Priest’s Robe, the Hair of the Ancient of Days, Eyes Like Fire, the Sword from His Mouth (Rev 1:12–17)

예수님을 가장 잘 알던 제자 요한이 왜 그 발 앞에 죽은 자같이 엎드러졌.en: Why did John, the disciple who knew Jesus best, fall at his feet as dead? The description in 1:12–17 is not a sketch of his appearance; it gathers pieces of Old Testament visions once used of God and sets them upon Jesus. The “garment down to the foot” (podērēs), found only once in the New Testament, is the high priest’s robe, and the girdle about the breast rather than the waist marks the one who has finished atonement and sat down (Heb 10:12). Hair white like wool is the description used of the Ancient of days, the Father, in Daniel 7:9, showing that the Son bears the Father’s eternity. Eyes as a flame of fire are eyes that search all things; feet like fine brass refined in a furnace are feet standing to judge, in the metal of judgment from the tabernacle’s outer court; a voice as the sound of many waters is the voice of the LORD in Ezekiel 43:2; and the sharp twoedged sword from his mouth is the word of truth from Isaiah 11 and 49. Reading on to how each of the seven churches in chapters 2–3 receives one face of this Christ, the lecture urges us to grow from a faith that saw only a Jesus abounding in love to a mature faith that gladly welcomes Jesus coming as Judge and King.

휴거 논쟁은 두 질문으로 정리됩니다 — 언제 일어나는가(환난 전·중·후·.en: The rapture debate comes down to two questions: when does it happen (pre-, mid-, posttribulation or pre-wrath), and who takes part (all believers, or only a watchful few)? First, comparing four interpretive traditions on the parable of the ten virgins, the key text of the partial-rapture view, every view except partial rapture agrees that “the five foolish are unbelievers.” The text itself says so: all ten virgins slumbered and slept, so watchfulness did not divide them; the oil is the Holy Spirit, and if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his (Rom 8:9); and the Lord’s reply, “I know you not,” is the same declaration made to unbelievers in Matthew 7:23. As grounds for a full rapture, we look at the repeated “all” in “we shall all be changed” (1 Cor 15:51), spoken to the quarrelsome Corinthian church; 1 Thessalonians 5:10, “whether we wake or sleep, we should live together with him”; and the judgment seat that decides rewards (1 Cor 3:15). Next comes the timing of the Rapture: why the last trump cannot be identified with the seventh trumpet of Revelation; the wrath of the Lamb already proclaimed at the sixth seal (Rev 6:16–17); five grounds for a pretribulation rapture (the prepositional structure of tēreō ek, 1 Thess 5:9, the absence of the word “church” in Revelation 4–18, Daniel’s seventy weeks as Israel’s timetable, and the removal of the restrainer); and the difficulty of a posttribulation rapture (the natural people of the Millennium in Isa 65:20). After explaining why “taken” in Matthew 24 means judgment rather than the Rapture (Luke 17:37) and the Rapture’s true home in the upper-room promise (John 14:2–3), there is one conclusion: this doctrine is meant not for date-setting or fear but for comfort (1 Thess 4:18).

요한계시록 스토리 09 · 사망과 음부의 열쇠의 비밀 — 두려워하지 말라.en: Revelation Story 09 · The Secret of the Keys of Hell and of Death — Fear Not, the Door of Death Is in the Lord’s Hand (Rev 1:17–20)

예수님의 가슴에 기대던 요한이 영광 중의 주님 앞에서 죽은 자같이 엎드러.en: John, who once leaned on Jesus’ breast, falls as dead before the Lord in his glory — just as Isaiah, Ezekiel and Daniel did. Laying his right hand on John, the Lord says, “Fear not; I am the first and the last.” “The first and the last” is a title the LORD used of himself alone in Isaiah 41, 44 and 48, and the New Testament writers consistently apply passages about the LORD to Jesus (Joel 2:32 → Rom 10:13, Isa 45:23 → Phil 2:10, Isa 8:13 → 1 Pet 3:15, Psalm 102 → Heb 1:10). The keys of resurrection, which Jewish tradition said God alone holds (Deut 32:39, 1 Sam 2:6), Jesus says he has — not because he picked the lock from outside, but because he entered death himself, broke its door from within and came out (Hos 13:14 → 1 Cor 15:55, Heb 2:14). The lecture distinguishes Hades (the intermediate place, rendered “hell” in the KJV) from Gehenna (final hell), looks at the two compartments of Luke 16, three views of Christ’s descent into Hades, and the texts showing that New Testament saints are at once with the Lord when they die (2 Cor 5:8, Phil 1:23). It then traces four times these keys turn in the flow of Revelation (the Rapture, the two witnesses, the Tribulation saints, the great white throne) and on to “The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death” (1 Cor 15:26). Verse 19 is the blueprint of all of Revelation (the things seen, the things which are, the things hereafter), and in the mystery of the seven stars the angels are the pastors of each church — a fear and also a safety, since those entrusted with the Word are in the Lord’s right hand. “Fear not” is not sentiment but fact: the keys to the door of death are in the hand of the One who loves me (Heb 2:15).

요한계시록 스토리 10 · 신천지가 훔쳐간 단어 '이기는 자' — 처음.en: Revelation Story 10 · “He That Overcometh,” the Word the Shincheonji Cult Stole — Ephesus, the Church That Left Its First Love (Rev 2:1–7)

2만 5천 석 대극장은 관광지로 남았는데, 바울·디모데·요한이 섬긴 1세.en: The great theater of 25,000 seats survives as a tourist site, so why did the church of Ephesus — the strongest church of the first century, served by Paul, Timothy and John — vanish completely? Starting from the seven-step blueprint of the letters to the seven churches (recipient → sender → commendation → rebuke → counsel → “let him hear” → reward) and the way the chapter 1 vision becomes a doctor’s prescription for each church, the lecture shows how an orthodox church praised for its works, labor and patience, and even for the discernment to expose false apostles, left its first love (the bridal love of Jer 2:2) within a single generation (33 years). The prescription is not a feeling but action: remember, repent, and do the first works. It then sets right the word that a heretical group stole, “he that overcometh.” It is not a title claimed by one cult leader; as 1 John 5:4–5 defines it, it is every born-again believer who believes that Jesus is the Son of God, and the original ho nikōn is a collective expression like “whosoever believeth” (John 3:16) that appears in every one of the seven letters. The reward is the reopening of the tree of life, closed since Eden (Gen 3:24 → Rev 2:7). After two interpretations of the Nicolaitans (a licentious sect / nikaō + laos, a power that lords it over the people) and the five stages by which an orthodox church dies (beginning in love → defending truth → love growing cold → truth without love → the candlestick removed), it closes with three practices: examining the heart, gently admonishing with 1 John 5:4–5, and immediately restoring one first work. A church dies not from heretical doctrine but from the loss of love.

주후 155년 화형대에서 '86년간 그분은 나를 해치신 적이 없는데 어찌.en: Smyrna was the city of Polycarp, who at the stake in AD 155 answered, “Eighty-six years I have served him, and he has done me no wrong; how can I blaspheme my King?” Of the seven churches, the one praised without rebuke (together with Philadelphia) was the poorest and most persecuted. The city’s name, Smyrna, means myrrh, which gives off its fragrance only when crushed, and myrrh’s four uses — the tabernacle’s anointing oil (Exod 30), the gift at his birth (Matt 2), the wine refused at the cross (Mark 15) and the burial spices (John 19) — trace the path of Christ. In the leading city of emperor worship, the sender is “the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive” (the LORD’s title in Isa 44:6) — the true Lord rather than Caesar, and, like the city that was destroyed and rebuilt, the guarantee of a resurrection that has passed through death. “I know thy works, and tribulation (thlipsis, crushing pressure), and poverty (ptōcheia, utter destitution), (but thou art rich)” — heaven’s ledger, the exact opposite of self-proclaimed rich Laodicea. “The synagogue of Satan” is no ground for anti-Semitism (the Jesus who spoke it and the John who wrote it were both Jews; Rom 11); it is an indictment of an assembly whose master had changed. They did the work of Satan, the accuser in the courtroom (Zech 3; Rev 12:10), by informing on believers to Rome and pushing them out from under the umbrella of a legal religion, and at Polycarp’s burning they carried firewood even on the Sabbath. With a warning that driving out believers who proclaim the true Word within today’s church is a modern form of that synagogue attitude, the lecture closes with a trial whose term is fixed, like Daniel’s ten days (Rev 2:10); the crown of life (stephanos), not the stone-built “crown of Asia”; and the victory of the overcomer, who may suffer the first death but shall not be hurt of the second death. The crown goes to those who stand on the Word, not on a signboard.

베를린 페르가몬 박물관에 복원된 제우스 대제단 — 예수님은 버가모를 '사.en: The Great Altar of Zeus, reconstructed in Berlin’s Pergamon Museum: Jesus called Pergamos the place “where Satan’s seat is” (Rev 2:13). In this city, which combined parchment, the temple of Asclepius, the altar of Zeus and Asia’s first temple of emperor worship, “Satan’s seat” is not one particular building but the whole combined system in which religion, politics, medicine and law join to cry, “We can live without God.” When three hundred years of persecution failed to break Smyrna, Satan changed his strategy: instead of killing, he seated believers at the table of idols — compromise and appeasement. The scheme of Balaam in Numbers, who failed to curse Israel and then brought it down by seduction (Num 31:16), worked in Pergamos through the idol feasts of the trade guilds and the rationalization that “believing in your heart is enough.” The lecture covers Paul’s discernment of the two tables (1 Cor 10: meat in the market is food, but the temple table is fellowship with devils); the Nicolaitans, who grew from “deeds” in Ephesus into a “doctrine” in Pergamos (nikaō + laos — a hierarchy lording it over the people); and the historical Pergamos era of church and empire in alliance after Constantine (AD 313–590). It closes with the overcomer’s three gifts: the hidden manna of the Holy of Holies (Christ the bread of life) instead of the guild’s perishing table; the white stone — acquittal, an admission ticket to the feast, a jewel of the breastplate — instead of the world court’s condemnation; and a new name known only to the Lord and the one who receives it, instead of the world’s registers that are published and inspected. The Lord with the sharp sword with two edges asks: under Satan’s seat, which table will you choose?

일곱 교회 도시 중 가장 작은 두아디라가 가장 긴 편지를 받았습니다 —.en: Thyatira, the smallest of the seven church cities, received the longest letter — because a woman “which calleth herself a prophetess,” whom the Lord named Jezebel, had come into the church and was teaching there. Yet the target of the rebuke is surprising: Jesus rebuked not the woman but **the church that tolerated her**. The lecture lays the background — a church that began with Lydia’s opened heart (Acts 16:14); a city where guild feasts were a matter of livelihood itself; Revelation’s only use of the title “the Son of God” (a proclamation to the city of Apollo, son of Zeus); and the Lord coming with feet of brass to a city of bronze-workers — and then examines the mirror structure with Ephesus (love without discernment ↔ discernment without love); three “self-proclaimed” titles (apostle, Jew, prophet — names no one can give himself); and four scenes of Jezebel in Kings (accepted through a political marriage · the table that fed 850 · the graves of true prophets · Naboth’s murder dressed in proper form). “The depths of Satan” (Rev 2:24) is praise for the remnant — a knowledge it is a blessing not to have (Rom 6:1–2) — and “none other burden” refers to the last two lines left by the Jerusalem council in Acts 15 (things offered to idols and fornication); Jezebel offered not a new freedom but the erasing of those lines. The judgment comes in three strands (the bed · the condition of repentance · the death of her children), and Thyatira in church history is the Middle Ages (590–1517) — which is why “till I come” appears for the first time among the seven letters. To the overcomer are promised authority over the nations from Psalm 2 (the rod of iron is a shepherd’s rod — the Millennium) and the morning star (Rev 22:16 — Jesus himself), the star seen before sunrise only by those who are awake — a picture of the Rapture. Love is no exemption from discernment.

요한계시록 스토리 14 · 생명책에서 이름이 지워질 수 있을까 — 살았다.en: Revelation Story 14 · Can Your Name Be Blotted Out of the Book of Life? — A Name That Lives, Sardis the Dead Church (Rev 3:1–6)

1년 내내 시들지 않는 꽃은 조화입니다 — 예수님은 행위도 평판도 있던.en: A flower that never wilts all year long is an artificial one. Jesus diagnosed the church at Sardis, which had both works and reputation: “thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead” (Rev 3:1). Against the background of the city of the first gold coins and of Croesus, an impregnable clifftop capital that was left with nothing but its name, the lecture looks at the One who has the seven Spirits (Isa 11:2); the two stages in Ezekiel’s valley (form → breath); and a church in which not even “Satan” appears — a thief does not rob an empty house. “As a thief” (Rev 3:3) is a word of discipline to a local church aimed at Sardis’s history of being captured twice while its guards slept; it is not a rapture verse. The prescription is remember → hold fast → repent: return to the first grace. The “few names” in the dead church guard the embers, and the white raiment is a gift with which God himself clothes us anew (Zech 3). Finally, “I will not blot out his name out of the book of life” (Rev 3:5) is not a warning that salvation can be cancelled but the strongest promise of the security of salvation in all seven letters.

요한계시록 스토리 15 · 환난 통과인가, 환난 전 건짐인가 — 빌라델비.en: Revelation Story 15 · Through the Tribulation, or Kept from It? — The Church in Philadelphia and Revelation 3:10

주후 17년 대지진 이후 늘 흔들리던 도시의 작은 교회에게 '성전의 기둥.en: To a small church in a city that had been shaking ever since the great earthquake of AD 17 comes a comfort made to measure: “Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out.” Passing through the three commendations of a church without rebuke (keeping the Word · not denying his name · the word of his patience), the key of David (Isa 22) and an Isaiah 60 turned upside down, the lecture enters 3:10, the most debated verse in church history. It is not the “temptation” but “the hour of temptation” from which they are kept; the biblical use of the preposition ek (Acts 15:29, 2 Cor 1:10, 1 Thess 1:10); why John 17:15 cannot serve as a counterexample (what is kept from is a person in one case and a time in the other); the purpose of the Great Tribulation (judgment of the world and the conversion of Israel); the Old Testament pattern of Enoch, Noah and Lot; and the arrangement of chapters 3–4, from an open door on earth to an open door in heaven (the absence of the church in chapters 4–19) — completing the case for being kept from the Tribulation in a single lecture.

요한계시록 스토리 16 · 미지근한 신앙에서 벗어나는 법 — 라오디게아.en: Revelation Story 16 · How to Escape Lukewarm Faith — The Church of the Laodiceans and a Summary of the Seven Churches

일곱 교회 시리즈의 마지막, 라오디게아 교회 강해. 북쪽 히에라볼리의 치.en: The last of the seven-churches series: an exposition of the church of the Laodiceans. Hierapolis to the north with its healing hot springs, Colossae to the east with its refreshing cold water, and Laodicea’s lukewarm, lime-laden water piped in from a distant spring — the water of these three cities first shows that “I would thou wert cold or hot” is a matter not of degrees of zeal but of usefulness. The lecture traces in turn how the pride of a wealthy banking city that declined Rome’s help to rebuild led to the boast “have need of nothing”; the Lord’s self-introduction as the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God (Isa 65:16, Col 1:15–18); “I will spue thee out of my mouth,” rooted in Leviticus; the prescription “buy of me,” aimed at the city’s three boasts (banking, black wool and eye salve); and the Lord standing at the door, read together with Song of Solomon 5. Finally, it sums up the seven churches in one table and closes with seven questions to examine ourselves today.

요한계시록 심화 01 · 계시록 6장 2절 흰 말 탄 자의 정체 — 그리.en: Revelation Deep Dive 01 · Who Is the Rider on the White Horse in Revelation 6:2 — Christ or the Antichrist?

성도의 질문에 답하는 심화 강의. 계시록 6장 2절의 흰 말 탄 자에게는.en: An in-depth lecture answering a question from believers. The rider on the white horse in Revelation 6:2 has a bow but no arrows, has no name, and takes nothing for himself (the passive edothē, “was given”). Read alongside a six-point contrast with the One on the white horse in chapter 19, the four horses of Zechariah, the four sore judgments of Ezekiel 14:21 and the parallel in the Olivet Discourse of Matthew 24, the first rider’s role is deception. The lecture also covers the arguments for the view that he is Christ, held by Irenaeus and others, with replies, and cautions that naming a living person is conspiracy theory.

요한계시록 심화 02 · 30분에 끝내는 열 처녀 비유 총정리 — 다섯.en: Revelation Deep Dive 02 · The Parable of the Ten Virgins in 30 Minutes — Who Are the Five Virgins, and Where Is the Marriage Feast Held? (Matt 25:1–13)

열 처녀 비유에서 생기는 두 질문 — 혼인 잔치에 못 들어간 다섯 처녀는.en: The parable of the ten virgins raises two questions: who are the five virgins who could not enter the marriage feast, and is the feast held in heaven right after the Rapture or on earth after the Second Coming? Read through the four stages of a Jewish wedding (betrothal · the bridegroom’s procession · the wedding · the feast), the betrothal is the church age, the procession is the Rapture (1 Thess 4:16–17), the wedding takes place in the air, and the marriage feast is held on earth after the Second Coming, with the seven-year Tribulation in between (note the distinction in Rev 19:7–9 between the marriage and “they which are called”). The bride, the church, is singular, while the ten virgins are plural: Jews going out to meet the Bridegroom during the seven-year Tribulation; and “the kingdom of heaven” is not the heaven we go to when we die but a reign on this earth. Since, as the words “go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves” show, oil cannot be bought and sold, we cannot nail it down as “A equals B”; as a secondary lesson it speaks of being filled with the Spirit and of grace. Salvation received in the age of grace is never cancelled. The lecture also covers the tactic of the Shincheonji cult, which stirs up fear of losing salvation by claiming “the oil is our doctrine”; two reasons established churches are helpless against it; and the principles that resolve it: the first recipients, and the distinction between the church and Israel.

요한계시록 심화 03 · 마지막 나팔과 일곱째 나팔은 같은 것인가 — 바.en: Revelation Deep Dive 03 · Are the Last Trump and the Seventh Trumpet the Same? — Paul’s Trumpet, John’s Trumpet and the Two Witnesses (1 Cor 15:52; Rev 11)

성경 종말론의 극적인 두 나팔 — 바울이 말한 교회 소망의 정점 '마지막.en: Two dramatic trumpets of biblical eschatology: is “the last trump” Paul spoke of, the high point of the church’s hope (1 Cor 15:52; 1 Thess 4:16), the same as “the seventh trumpet” John recorded, which announces the end of world history (Rev 11:15)? Passing through the structure of the seven trumpets (warnings striking a third of nature, and people who still do not repent — Rev 9:20–21), we reach the seventh trumpet, where instead of a plague a cosmic coronation is proclaimed: “The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ.” The lecture compares the two trumpets by function (gathering and transformation vs. proclamation and revelation), audience (the church vs. an unrepentant world) and result (the saints changed and meeting the Lord in the air vs. the start of the final wrath), and shows how identifying them or not connects with the posttribulation and pretribulation rapture views. It then turns to the two witnesses who minister just before the seventh trumpet — the legal principle of two witnesses in Deuteronomy 19:15, Moses and Elijah on the Mount of Transfiguration, and the two powers of Revelation 11:6 — and gives three reasons a symbolic reading breaks down (the location, Jerusalem; a judgment ministry with fire proceeding out of their mouth; a period of 1,260 days). From God’s timetable, under which not even the beast can touch them before they finish their testimony, to the world’s frenzy of exchanging gifts over their bodies, the live broadcast of their resurrection after three and a half days, and the ark of the covenant in the heavenly temple, it closes by showing why the reading that “prophecy is already finished” is the method of interpretation Satan likes best.

특강 · 120분 핵심정리 요한계시록 — 기초 · 필수 용어 · 오해 풀.en: Special Lecture · Revelation in 120 Minutes — Foundations · Essential Terms · Clearing Up Misconceptions (Stories 01–04 in One)

요한계시록 강해의 기초 과정인 스토리 01~04를 한 편으로 이어 붙인.en: A two-hour summary that joins Stories 01–04, the foundation course of the Revelation exposition, into a single video. Its four parts answer four questions in turn. Part 1, “Why should we read it?” — the only book in the Bible that promises a blessing for reading it, the “revelation” (apokalypsis) that lifts the veil. Part 2, “How is it structured?” — the table of contents Jesus himself gave in 1:19 (the things seen · the things which are · the things hereafter), the map of all 22 chapters, and the “church” that disappears from the earth after 4:1. Part 3, “Which terms must we know first?” — how the word Rapture (harpazō) came to be translated, six contrasts between the Rapture and the Second Coming, and the end-time timeline in one line. Part 4, “What must we clear away?” — the fear of Revelation left by the 1992 rapture scare, seven misconceptions, and the test for weighing views: “Does it awaken a sense of imminence, or dull it?” Finish this one video and you are ready to follow the verse-by-verse exposition that begins at 1:4.

특강 · 180분 몰아보기 요한계시록 1장 — 삼위의 인사에서 사망과 음.en: Special Lecture · Revelation Chapter 1 in 180 Minutes — From the Triune Greeting to the Keys of Hell and of Death (Stories 05–09)

요한계시록 1장을 다룬 스토리 연작(05~09)을 한 호흡으로 묶은 16.en: A 161-minute complete summary that gathers the story series on Revelation 1 (05–09) in one sitting: the greeting of the triune God and Jesus’ three titles (vv. 4–6); the declaration of a visible Second Coming that every eye will see, and the ultimate rapture debate (v. 7); the Alpha and Omega who bears the LORD’s exclusive name (vv. 8, 11); the seven features of the Son of man walking among the candlesticks and their Old Testament roots (vv. 12–16); three grounds for “Fear not” and the keys of hell and of death (vv. 17–18); and the three-part blueprint of all of Revelation (v. 19). Here you can run the whole map of chapter 1 — “know this and the Bible opens” — in one place. For beginners it is a map for crossing the threshold of Revelation; for those who have watched the series, a complete review course.

인자 환상.en: Vision of the Son of Man

선악과 비밀 01 · 선악과는 진짜 과일이었을까? 독이 없는데 아담은 왜.en: Forbidden Fruit Secrets 01 · Was the Forbidden Fruit a Real Fruit? If It Wasn’t Poisonous, Why Did Adam Die?

선악과를 둘러싼 네 가지 해석 — 알레고리, 성적 타락설, 자유주의 신화.en: This lecture compares four interpretations of the forbidden fruit — allegory, the sexual-fall theory, liberal myth theory, and the historical, literal reading — and shows that the tree of the knowledge of good and evil was a real tree, on the grounds of Genesis’s grammar of historical narrative, the citations by Jesus and Paul, and the Adam–Christ parallel in Romans 5. What killed Adam was not some substance in the fruit but the covenant word, “in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die,” and the tree was not a trap set for a fall but a boundary stone marking God’s sovereignty and a sign that made freely given love possible.

선악과 비밀 02 · '선악을 알게 되었다'의 진짜 뜻 — 아담은 무지하.en: Forbidden Fruit Secrets 02 · The Real Meaning of “Knowing Good and Evil” — Adam Was Not Ignorant

명령을 받은 아담은 무지 상태가 아니라 무죄 상태였습니다. 히브리어 '야.en: Adam, who received the command, was not in a state of ignorance but of innocence. From the Hebrew yada (knowing by experience) and its use in Deuteronomy 1:39, 2 Samuel 14:17 and 1 Kings 3:9, the lecture shows that “to know good and evil” is an idiom for the authority to judge and decide, and that the essence of the Fall was not curiosity but a rebellion that seized God’s right to judge. It covers Satan’s three-step temptation, the wordplay between “naked” and “subtil,” death as separation, and coats of skins rather than fig leaves — the gospel of atonement already foreshadowed in Eden.

선악과 비밀 특별강의 · 루시퍼는 아담보다 먼저 타락했다? — 역사적 아.en: Forbidden Fruit Secrets Special Lecture · Did Lucifer Fall Before Adam? — The Historical Adam, the Origin of Sin and the Gap Theory

아담은 신화인가 역사인가 — 유신진화론의 도전 앞에서 성경 내적 증거(역.en: Is Adam myth or history? Facing the challenge of theistic evolution, this lecture defends the historical Adam with internal biblical evidence (the genealogies of Chronicles, Jesus’ citations, the culmination of Luke’s genealogy, Paul’s two-Adam framework) and three pillars of systematic theology (the doctrine of original sin, the Christological argument that a symbolic problem would need only a symbolic salvation, and the authority of Scripture). It then asks, “Then who started sin?” — the verb “entered” in Romans 5:12; the nature of sin (not a substance but a lack, a departure from the order of creation); the process by which lust conceives and brings forth sin (Jas 1:14–15); the timing of the angels’ creation in Job 38 and the Bible’s silence on when Lucifer fell; and why the gap theory, which inserts hundreds of millions of years and a judgment between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2, is an imaginative reading at odds with the grammar of the text and with sound theology.

선악과 비밀 03 · 하나님이 악을 창조하셨는가? — 이사야 45장 7절.en: Forbidden Fruit Secrets 03 · Did God Create Evil? — Reading Isaiah 45:7 Rightly

무신론자들이 내미는 이사야 45:7 '평안도 짓고 환난도 창조하나니'를.en: Isaiah 45:7, “I make peace, and create evil,” which atheists hold up as an objection, is read rightly through parallelism and context (Cyrus and the judgment of Babylon), and Ezekiel 28 and Isaiah 14 show that evil is not a substance but a lack of good and a rebellion that arose within created persons. God is not the author of evil but its Ruler and Conqueror. The lecture closes the trilogy with the bookends of the whole Bible: the garden and the tree where the first Adam failed are reclaimed by the last Adam, Jesus, at Gethsemane and the cross, and brought to completion in the tree of life of Revelation 22.

특강 · 60분 완전정리 선악과 — 왜 하나님은 넘어질 나무를 두셨나(선.en: Special Lecture · The Forbidden Fruit Fully Explained in 60 Minutes — Why Did God Place a Tree We Could Stumble Over? (Forbidden Fruit Secrets 01–03 in One)

선악과 비밀 01~03을 한 편으로 이어 붙인 60분 완전정리입니다. 1.en: A 60-minute complete summary joining Forbidden Fruit Secrets 01–03 into one video. Part 1, “Was it a real tree, and why did Adam die?” — four interpretations, and the tree as a sign of the covenant. Part 2, “What does ‘knowing good and evil’ mean?” — knowing by experience, the seizing of the right to judge, and the gospel of the coats of skins. Part 3, “Did God create evil?” — reading Isaiah 45:7 rightly, evil as both lack and rebellion, and the first Adam and the last Adam. Recommended for anyone who wants to review the whole series at once.
